properties.name: MEASURED (Grok Build 1.0.30, this box, 2026-09-20): `grok mcp list` run inside a project holding a valid reflow2 .mcp.json answers "No MCP servers configured" — Grok reads ~/.grok/config.toml or ./.grok/config.toml, in TOML, so the harness alias grok→claude writes a file Grok never opens
properties.statement: SYMPTOM AS REPORTED, second-hand: Alex, at home on Grok Build, starting a NEW project — the .reflow2 folder gets created, then Grok reports the MCP server is not registered for that project. He asked whether he must run something like "reflow2 --init" per project. THE MEASUREMENT, taken on this box 2026-09-20 against Grok Build 1.0.30, the same product and version already characterised in fact:grok-build-measured-on-this-box-it-hands-the-model-only-the-text-block-and-hides-mcp-tools-behind-a-search. Run inside /home/ajs7/project/reflow2, which holds a valid .mcp.json declaring the reflow2 stdio server, `grok mcp list` answers: "No MCP servers configured. Run `grok mcp add --help` to get started." Its own help states its two sources, and neither is .mcp.json: "user: ~/.grok/config.toml, available in all your projects" and "project: ./.grok/config.toml, shared with everyone working in this directory". Confirmed end to end in a scratch directory: `grok mcp add reflow2 --scope project -- <binary> --graph-path ./.reflow2/graph --shared` wrote a TOML block [mcp_servers.reflow2] into ./.grok/config.toml, and `grok mcp list` then printed the server. So the registration path works; it is simply a different file in a different format from the one reflow2 writes. WHAT THIS REFUTES IN THE SOURCE. tools/reflow2_init.py resolves the harness name "grok" to "claude" through HARNESS_ALIASES, on the stated ground that "Grok CLI reads .mcp.json, so it is served by claude", and its config-writer comment repeats it: ".mcp.json — Claude Code (Grok CLI also loads it as a compatibility source, so this one file covers both)". AGENTS-facing prose says the same. For Grok Build 1.0.30 that is false. A user who answers "grok" to --harness therefore gets .mcp.json, .reflow2/ and a pointer file, and nothing Grok will ever open — which presents to the agent as reflow2 not being registered for the project, exactly as reported. ⭐ THE CLASS, AND IT IS VISIBLE IN THE SAME FILE. Twelve lines below the grok alias sits the Copilot entry, and it is exemplary: "MEASURED 2026-08-14, not assumed. `copilot mcp --help` states its sources... confirmed end to end: `copilot mcp list`, run inside a project set up by this installer, printed 'Workspace servers: reflow2 (local)'." The grok alias was added the same week, and its recorded reason is a fact about the PERSON — "on learning the second user runs Grok at home and Claude at work" — not a measurement of the CLIENT. So the class is that reflow2 asserts where other products keep their MCP configuration, one product at a time, with no check; the neighbour was measured and this one rode along on an assumption. A fix that only adds a grok entry leaves the next client to be guessed at. WHAT WOULD PIN IT: a gate that, for every harness the installer claims to serve, runs that product's own list command inside a directory the installer has just set up and fails if the product does not report the server. It cannot run in CI where those binaries are absent, so the honest form is a local instrument plus a recorded per-client measurement date, in the shape check_doc_versions already uses for version claims. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CAUSE IS ALSO LIVE and must not be collapsed into this one: fact:field-report-genesis-on-grok-build-cannot-finish-because-next-step-names-mcp-and-the-latent-server-is-never-replaced records Alex hitting the same PRESENTATION on 2026-09-14 at v0.60.2, where reflow2_start_design created an empty .reflow2/ and the latent two-tool surface was never promoted. That was fixed in v0.61.0 and is superseded. If Alex is below v0.61.0 it alone explains the report; if he is at or above it, this config-location defect does. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ONE COMMAND, and it is his to run in the new project: `grok mcp doctor`, or `grok mcp list`. No reflow2 listed means the config never reached Grok, which is this finding. reflow2 listed but only a tool or two served means the latent surface never promoted, which is the older one. NOT ESTABLISHED: Alex's installed reflow2 version; how he registered reflow2 on Grok in the first place, since the installer has no Grok path at all and reflow2_install.py contains no occurrence of the string; whether Grok CLI, a different product from Grok Build, ever read .mcp.json as the source claims; and the exact wording of his report, which arrived paraphrased through Anthony. ⚠️ ONE THING IS SETTLED EITHER WAY: running an init per project is NOT the missing step. Init writes .mcp.json, which Grok does not read. The step that works on Grok is `grok mcp add`.
